thread:
olivia: Heads-up — NimbleSI flagged a billing discrepancy after their nightly usage push. We have negative deltas for a handful of customers (credits applied and then removed). Looks tied to their webhook retries around 00:00 PST.
marcel: Ugh. Are we seeing duplicate usage events or a reconciliation mismatch?
samir: Initial look: their payloads are fine, but our marketplace-ingest service is deduping on an event_id that NimbleSI rotates when TTL crosses midnight in their infra. So the same logical usage ends up with two different event_ids, we ingest both, then the entitlement service rolls one back during the next reconciliation window.
olivia: that matches the customer reports — short-lived double credit then a reversal. A few customers already pinged partner-success.
angela: Can we confirm which component flips the final reversal? Is that entitlement-engine or ledger-backfill?
samir: entitlement-engine enforces seat/entitlement caps during daily reconcile; ledger-backend records events raw. Sequence is: market-ingest -> ledger -> entitlement reconcile job (23:59-00:10) -> occasionally a correction job (00:30) that removes the earlier duplicate once the true start_time is reconciled.
marcel: So root cause is NimbleSI's per-event id strategy + our dedupe key. Need a durable idempotency approach between partners.
olivia: Agreed. Proposed short-term mitigation: treat NimbleSI webhooks as non-unique by event_id alone — use (event_id || partner_upload_id || payload.hash) as dedupe key for 48h. Longer-term: require partners to send idempotency-key header or stable event ids.
samir: I pushed a small patch to marketplace-ingest to fallback to payload checksum when event_id changes within 5m of the same usage window. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-ingest/pull/424 (WIP). The checksum logic is: 
```
const checksum = sha256(JSON.stringify({customer_id, usage_window_start, usage_value}));
if (seen(event.event_id) || seen(checksum)) skip(); else persist();
```
marcel: Please add partner tag in logs so we can query quickly: `partner_nimblesi` as a field.
samir: will do. Deploy plan: canary to 10% traffic in us-west-2, monitor for duplicate-count metric. angela canary?
angela: I'll roll canary at 03:15 UTC after the next nightly push. Deploy-bot: create canary and report health.
deploy-bot: Canary started for marketplace-ingest@canary-216123 — 10% in us-west-2.
olivia: Partner comms: @partner-success can you notify NimbleSI that we're applying a transient dedupe tolerance and ask them to switch to sending a stable `Idempotency-Key` HTTP header. Also ask for their SDK version; earlier versions have this midnight-ttl bug.
partner-success: On it — pinged NimbleSI PM (cc'd) with the mitigation and asking for timeline. They said they'll prioritize a fix but need a one-week window.
marcel: Action items: 1) samir - finish PR + add partner tag + unit tests (ETA 6h), 2) angela - canary deploy + monitor duplicate-count & negative-ledger-deltas (ETA 4h), 3) partner-success - partner comms + ask for SDK version + prod timeline (ETA 1h), 4) olivia - prepare rollback/backfill playbook if canary shows regressions (ETA 6h).
samir: Tests added, pushed new commit with logging fields. Running integration now.
angela: Canary healthy so far (30m). duplicate-count metric down from 18/hr to 1/hr for NimbleSI traffic.
olivia: Good sign. If numbers stay low after full rollout, we should run a focused backfill to correct the small set of affected accounts rather than bulk ledger rewrites.
marcel: Agreed — create a backfill job that reverses only pairs where checksum matches and timestamps within 2m. Keep audit trail.
partner-success: NimbleSI replied: they will push SDK patch by next Tue and can temporarily add stable header by EOD. They appreciate the canary.
deploy-bot: Canary completed. marketplace-ingest@canary-216123 -> canary success.
samir: I'll open the backfill job PR and a postmortem draft for board of partners. Link when ready.
olivia: Thanks team. I'll draft a short external note for affected customers after we have final numbers.
marcel: Nice triage — keep thread updated with PRs and backfill job id.
partner-success: Will update NimbleSI and share SDK version when they confirm.
olivia: Closing loop: once SDK + header in place and one full nightly reconcile passes with zero new reversals, we mark as resolved and run the targeted backfill.
marcel: tagging for follow-up: #billing, #sre, #partnerships.
